Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 107, verse 1:

We begin this session with the explanation of the words of Allah, blessed and exalted be He: ﴿Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense? (1) For that is the one who pushes away the orphan﴾ [Al-Ma'un: 1, 2], to the end of the surah, God willing.

Allah, blessed and exalted be He, says: ﴿Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense?﴾ [Al-Ma'un: 1]. "Have you seen" (ara'ayta) is an address, but to whom? Is it addressed to the Messenger (ﷺ), since he is the one to whom the Qur'an was revealed, or is it general for everyone to whom the address is directed? The general meaning is more appropriate, so we say: "Have you seen the one who" is general for everyone to whom the address is directed.

"Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense?" That is, denies the reward (al-jaza'). These are the people who deny the Resurrection (al-ba'th) and say: ﴿When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected? And our forefathers, the earliest ones?﴾ [As-Saffat: 16, 17], and one of them says: ﴿Who will give life to the bones when they are decayed?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 78]. These are the ones who deny the Day of Recompense (al-Din). "Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense?" That is, denies the reward.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 107, verse 2–3:

﴿That is the one who repulses the orphan﴾ [al-Ma'un: 2, 3] So he combined two matters:

The first matter: lack of mercy toward orphans, who are the object of mercy. The orphans are those whose fathers died before they reached maturity, and they are the object of compassion and mercy, because he has lost his father; his heart is broken and in need of mending. For this reason the texts have come concerning the virtue of kindness to orphans. But this one—and we seek refuge in Allah—﴿repulses the orphan﴾, meaning he pushes him away violently, because al-da' (da') is pushing away with violence, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿On the Day they will be pushed toward the fire of Hell with a violent pushing﴾ [al-Tur: 13], meaning a forceful push. So you will find that when the orphan comes to him, asking him for something or speaking to him about some matter, he belittles him and pushes him away harshly, and shows him no mercy.

Also: they do not urge one another to show mercy to others: ﴿and does not urge the feeding of the needy﴾. So the poor, needy person who requires food is not urged by this man to feed him, because his heart is a stone, and we seek refuge in Allah; it is hard. Their hearts are like stones or even harder in hardness. Thus there is no mercy in him either toward orphans or toward the needy; he is hard-hearted, and we seek refuge in Allah.

**Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿So woe to those who pray﴾ [Al-Ma'un 4]. (Wayl) is a word of warning, and it is repeated often in the Qur'an; its meaning is a severe warning for these people.**

**﴿Who are heedless of their prayer﴾ [Al-Ma'un 4, 5]. These are people who pray, praying with the people or alone, but they are ﴿heedless of their prayer﴾, meaning they are negligent of it. They do not perform it as it should be performed: they delay it beyond its preferred time, they do not perfect its bowing, its prostration, its standing, or its sitting, and they do not recite what must be recited in it, whether Qur'an or dhikr. When one enters his prayer, he is inattentive, his heart wandering right and left, so he is heedless in his prayer. This is blameworthy. The one who forgets about prayer, neglects it and treats it lightly is without doubt blameworthy. As for the one who is forgetful within his prayer, he is not blamed. The difference between the two is that forgetfulness in prayer means that he has forgotten something: he forgot the number of rak'ahs, forgot some of the obligatory acts, and similar things. For this reason, forgetfulness occurred from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), though he was the most devoted of people to his prayer. Indeed, he (ﷺ) said: "The coolness of my eyes has been placed in prayer" [Narrated by al-Nasa'i (3940) and Ahmad (14037), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)], and yet he forgot in his prayer, because forgetfulness regarding something means that he forgot it in a manner for which he is not blamed. As for the one who is heedless of his prayer, he is deliberately neglectful in his prayer. Among heedlessness regarding prayer are those people who abandon prayer in congregation, for they are without doubt heedless of their prayer, and so they fall under this warning: ﴿So woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer﴾.**

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 107, verse 6:

﴿Those who make show [of their deeds]﴾ [al-Ma'un: 6, 7]. Also, when they perform an act of obedience, they intend by it only to ingratiate themselves with people and to gain standing in society; their aim is not drawing near to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. This show-off – and we seek refuge in Allah – gives charity so that people will say, "How generous he is!" This one who prays performs his prayer well so that people will say, "How well he prays!" and the like. These are the ones who show off. The origin of the act of worship is for Allah, but they also want people to praise them for it, and they draw near to people by means of their drawing near to Allah. These are the show-offs, and we seek refuge in Allah.

As for one who prays for the sake of people, meaning that he prays before a king, for example, or someone else, bowing or prostrating to him, this one is a polytheist and a disbeliever; Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his abode is the Fire.

But this one prays to Allah while being mindful that people should praise him for his worship, that he is a worshipper of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. This occurs frequently among the hypocrites, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when they stand up to prayer, they stand up lazily, showing off to the people and not remembering Allah except a little﴾ [an-Nisa': 142]. Observe this description: ﴿when they stand up to prayer, they stand up lazily﴾; so they are heedless of their prayer, ﴿showing off to the people﴾.

Here He says: ﴿Those who make show﴾. If someone says: Are those who make their deeds heard (the one who seeks to be heard, sami'a) like them? That is, a person, for example, recites the Qur'an, recites aloud, beautifies the recitation, beautifies the delivery and voice so that it may be said, "How well he recites!" Would he be like those who show off?

The answer: Yes, as came in the hadith: «Whoever makes his deed heard, Allah will make him heard [of his shame], and whoever shows off, Allah will show him off»[[Narrated by Muslim (2986/47) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]. The meaning: whoever makes his deed heard, Allah will expose him and make clear to people that the man is not sincere, but rather he wants people to hear of him so that they praise him for his worship; and whoever shows off, likewise, Allah will show him off. So the person who shows off to people or makes his deeds heard to people, Allah will expose him, and his affair will become clear, sooner or later.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 107, verse 7:

﴿Those who make show (of their deeds)﴾ [107:6]. ﴿And withhold (simple) assistance﴾ [107:7]. That is: they withhold what is obligatory to give of the utensils (al-mawa'in), which are the vessels (al-awani). That is, a person comes to them asking to borrow a vessel, saying: "I need a bucket, I need a container to drink from, I need an electric lamp and the like," and they refuse. This too is blameworthy.

Withholding al-ma'un is divided into two categories. One category is one for which a person incurs sin, and another category is one for which a person does not incur sin but misses out on good. So what it is obligatory to give, the person sins by withholding it; and what it is not obligatory to give, the person does not sin by withholding it, but he misses out on the good.

An example of this: a person comes to someone who is in dire need, saying: "Give me a vessel to drink from, for if I do not drink, I will die." Giving him the vessel is what? It is obligatory, and the person sins by withholding it. Indeed, some scholars say: if this person dies, the one who refused must pay blood money (diyah) for him, because he was the cause of what befell him, and it is obligatory for him to give what was requested.

Someone comes to another and says: "Give me a garment to warm me against the cold, or I will perish." Here it is obligatory for him to give him that garment, as an obligation.

However, the scholars differed on this matter: is it obligatory for the borrower in this situation to give the lender a fee (ujrah), or is it not obligatory? Or is it obligatory for usufructs (al-manafi') but not for the items themselves (al-a'yan)? How is this? For example, a person comes to you who is in dire need of food; if you do not feed him, he will perish. Here it is obligatory for you to feed him, but is it obligatory for him to give you the value of the food?

Some people of knowledge said: it is obligatory for him to give you the value of the food. Others said: it is not obligatory, because feeding him in this situation is an obligation upon you from God, and this view is the stronger one: that there is no compensation for it, because rescuing someone who is facing destruction is obligatory, and a person cannot take a wage for what God has made obligatory upon him.

On the second question: someone comes to you who is in need of a garment for fear of the cold, and you give him the garment. Is he obligated to pay a rent (ujrah) for this garment?

Some scholars say: he is obligated to pay a rent, and others say: he is not obligated. The correct view is that he is not obligated to pay the rent. But if you gave it to him by way of ownership (tamlik), then it is his property; and if you gave it to him by way of lending (ariyyah), then when he finds another garment, he is obligated to return it to you. This is the correct view. With this, the discussion of this surah concludes.

So a person must examine himself: is he among those who have characterized themselves by these traits or not? If he is among those who have characterized themselves by these traits, who have neglected the prayer, were heedless of it, and withheld good from others, then let him receive the good news of woe, and we seek refuge in God. And if he has remained free of that, then let him receive the good news of good.

The Noble Qur'an is not intended merely to be recited by a person as an act of worship through its recitation; rather, the purpose is that one be disciplined by it. For this reason 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "Indeed the Prophet (ﷺ) had as his character (khuluq) the Qur'an." (Khuluquhu) means his manners (akhlaq) which he adopted, taking them from the Qur'an. May Allah grant us and you success in what is good and righteous in this world and the Hereafter.
